name: Beechcraft Baron
summary: High-performance four-to-six-seat piston twin in production since 1961, a benchmark owner-flown and training twin.

engines: Two flat-six engines in slim, rounded nacelles
fuselage: Sleek rounded fuselage with a long pointed nose
Model 58 has double doors at the rear right
tail: Swept fin with conventional low horizontal tail

tellTales: Sleek, rounded-fuselage light twin with a conventional low tail
Plain wingtips with no tip tanks

confusedWith.howToTell: The Seneca has a shorter, blunter nose and a single-engine-style cabin; the Baron is sleeker with a long pointed nose.
The 310 has wingtip fuel tanks; the Baron has plain wingtips.
The Seminole has a T-tail; the Baron has a conventional low tail.
The DA42 is a composite twin with long slender wings and a T-tail.
The Travel Air looks like a smaller Baron but has a tall, upright, squared-off fin; the Baron's fin is swept back and its cabin and engines are larger.
The Duke is a bigger, pressurized six-seater with a rounder fuselage, small rounded windows and large three-blade props; the Baron is smaller and sleeker.
